haiku-low.q1: If the unfiltered row_count is 10,000 or fewer, the CSV returns directly in the 200 response. Above 10,000, a background job runs and the user gets an emailed link.
haiku-low.q2: The partial unique index blocks the second active insert. The API returns 200 with the existing queued or running export's id and status, and queues nothing.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed signed link works for 24 hours. The bucket lifecycle rule deletes the finished file 7 days after creation. Incomplete uploads are discarded after 24 hours.
haiku-low.q4: Up to three attempts, with retries after 60 s and 300 s. After the last failure, the row is marked failed, the page shows a failure message, and a failure email is sent.
haiku-low.q5: Both the direct and the background export paths read report rows from the read replica.
haiku-low.q6: Stored in the report_exports table in the primary database. The page polls every 5 seconds while active, and on reopen calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica, encodes them into an 8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, so memory holds only one batch and one buffer.
haiku-low.q8: On an exception, abort_multipart runs and the error is re-raised. If the worker dies or times out, the upload stays incomplete and invisible. The next attempt restarts from the first row with a new upload.
haiku-low.q9: They are stored as columns on the report_exports row, written at the click. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job reads the filters and columns from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status is queued or running. A violating insert makes the API return the existing active export instead.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be complete with object_key saved on the row before the email is sent. If the job runs again after succeeded or failed, it returns and does nothing.
haiku-low.q12: If the replica fails before bytes are sent, the API returns 503. If it fails mid-stream, the connection drops. The page saves no file, shows a failure message, and nothing retries automatically.

sonnet.q1: The API checks report.view and reads the unfiltered reports.row_count from the replica. 10,000 rows or fewer: CSV returned directly in the response (200, text/csv), page saves it as a file; no job, nothing stored. More than 10,000: API saves an export record, queues a background job, returns 202 with id and status queued; the job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails the user a link valid 24 hours.
sonnet.q2: The insert violates the partial unique index (one queued/running export per user per report). The API returns 200 with the existing export's id and status and queues nothing.
sonnet.q3: The link works 24 hours. The bucket's lifecycle rule deletes the stored file 7 days after creation (no cleanup job needed).
sonnet.q4: Three attempts (retries wait 60 s, then 300 s). After attempt 3 fails, on_final_failure sets status failed (with error and finished_at), then emails report_export_failed; the page shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.' and the user can click again to start a new export. If the failure email fails, it is logged only.
sonnet.q6: In the status column of the report_exports row in the primary database. The page polls GET /api/exports/{export_id} every 5 seconds while queued/running. On reopening, the page calls GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest to get the user's newest export, then polls if still active. The page keeps no state of its own.
sonnet.q7: It streams: reads 5,000 rows at a time from the replica (keyset by row_id), encodes to CSV in an in-memory buffer, and uploads each 8 MB as a multipart part, emptying the buffer. Memory holds at most one batch plus one 8 MB buffer. About 115 parts, a few minutes, within the 30-minute timeout. (The document does not mention a 512 MB worker specifically.)
sonnet.q8: On an exception the job calls abort_multipart and re-raises. If the worker crashes or times out, the upload is never completed, nothing becomes visible, and the bucket discards it after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts at step 6 with a new multipart upload from the first row; nothing carries over. (If complete_multipart succeeded but saving object_key failed, the next attempt rewrites the file and complete_multipart replaces it.)
sonnet.q9: They are stored (frozen) on the report_exports row in the primary database as filters and columns. The job payload carries only export_id, and the job loads the row to get them.
sonnet.q10: The partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where status in ('queued','running') in the report_exports table, created in step 1.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete, with complete_multipart done and object_key saved on the row. On a rerun: if the row is succeeded or failed, the job returns and does nothing. If the row is running with object_key set, it skips writing and goes straight to step 8 (signed URL and email), so if the file is finished but not marked succeeded, only the email is sent (possibly a second harmless email).
sonnet.q12: If the replica fails before any bytes are sent, the API returns 503. If it fails mid-stream, the API drops the connection. Either way the page saves no file and shows 'Export failed. Click Download CSV to try again.' Nothing retries automatically; no record, job or file exists.
